title: Per-series log volume with expected bands
description: Return log volume for every (namespace, environment, severity) series of one service, each with an expected band learned from the same time of week over the previous weeks of the volume rollup. This is the data behind the Anomalies tab in the logs UI. A bucket whose observed count sits above upper or below lower fell outside the expected range. Ranges target 99% coverage of individual buckets, so an out-of-range bucket is a reason to investigate, not a confirmed incident. lower and upper are null while a series is still learning. band_ready_at gives the earliest end of a rolling window of the same length with enough earlier history. Waiting does not add earlier history to a fixed historical window; select a more recent window instead. Omit intervalMinutes and the grain is picked from the window (7 days gives 60 minutes, 1 day gives 15); pass 5, 15, 30 or 60 to choose. A series too sparse or too quiet for the requested grain comes back coarser, with its own interval_minutes and a coarsened_reason. Requires a serviceName (use logs-services-create or the resource attribute values tool to discover services). The window defaults to the last 7 days, may span at most 7 days, and may start at most 35 days ago. Synchronous and read only.

methodDocumentation.text: Returns log volume over the requested window for every (namespace, environment, severity) series of one service, with a time-of-week expected band derived from the prior weeks of the volume rollup. The window defaults to the last 7 days and may span at most 7 days. Synchronous and read only.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription:
Display grain in minutes for buckets and bands. One of 5, 15, 30, 60. The window may hold at most 500 buckets per series at the chosen grain, so a finer grain needs a shorter window. Omit it to let the window pick its grain, the coarsest that still cuts it into about 168 buckets. A series too sparse to read at this grain is returned at a coarser one; see each series' interval_minutes.

* `5` - 5
* `15` - 15
* `30` - 30
* `60` - 60

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription:
Why this series was too thin to read at the requested grain, or null when it was not. sparse: fewer than 20% of its buckets held any records. quiet: its non-empty buckets averaged under 5 records. A series that fails every rung is returned at the coarsest one. A series that a coarser rung has no rows for, or that the request's time budget cannot refetch, keeps the requested grain and still carries its reason.

* `sparse` - sparse
* `quiet` - quiet
